pharm: Competitive H2-receptor antagonist that reduces gastric acid secretion; notable inhibitor of multiple cytochrome P450 enzymes.
quick: Duodenal ulcer: 800 mg at bedtime (or 300 mg QID); GERD 800 mg BID
May take with or without food; avoid simultaneous antacids
Crosses placenta; use only if clearly needed
Excreted in breast milk; use with caution
Reduce dose in renal impairment (e.g., 300 mg q12h if CrCl <30)
May raise blood alcohol levels; avoid excess
Renal function; mental status in elderly/ill; drug interactions
summary: Cimetidine is a histamine H2-receptor antagonist that suppresses gastric acid secretion, used for duodenal and gastric ulcers, GERD, and pathological hypersecretory states. It is clinically distinctive as a potent inhibitor of several cytochrome P450 enzymes, causing many drug interactions, and has weak antiandrogenic effects (gynecomastia). Reversible confusional states can occur in elderly or severely ill patients; renal dose reduction is required.
indications: Short-term treatment of active duodenal ulcer
Maintenance therapy for duodenal ulcer at reduced dose after healing
Short-term treatment of active benign gastric ulcer
Pathological hypersecretory conditions (Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, systemic mastocytosis, multiple endocrine adenomas)

dosage.n: Alternatives 300 mg QID or 400 mg BID; usually 4-8 weeks

dosage.d: 800 mg at bedtime or 300 mg QID
300 mg QID with meals and at bedtime

dosage.n: Adjust further per response; reduce dose with severe impairment

admin: Take orally with or without food
Do not give antacids simultaneously - they reduce cimetidine absorption; separate dosing
For ulcers a single bedtime dose suppresses nocturnal acid effectively
moa: Competitively and reversibly inhibits histamine at the H2 receptors of gastric parietal cells, reducing basal and stimulated (food, histamine, pentagastrin, caffeine, insulin) gastric acid secretion; it is not an anticholinergic agent.

relative: Concomitant narrow-therapeutic-index CYP substrates (warfarin, phenytoin, theophylline)

preg: Crosses the placenta; no clear evidence of fetal harm but use only if clearly needed (historically pregnancy category B).
lact: Excreted in human breast milk and concentrated there; use with caution or consider an alternative.
renal: Primarily renally eliminated; reduce dose in renal impairment (e.g., 300 mg every 12 hours for CrCl <30 mL/min) to avoid accumulation and CNS effects.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; combined hepatic and renal impairment further reduces clearance.

major: Warfarin - inhibits metabolism, raises INR/bleeding risk
moderate: Beta-blockers (propranolol), tricyclic antidepressants, benzodiazepines (chlordiazepoxide, diazepam), nifedipine, metronidazole - reduced clearance
Drugs needing gastric acidity (ketoconazole, atazanavir) - reduced absorption
interactions.food: May take with or without food; separate from antacids which impair absorption
interactions.alcohol: May increase blood alcohol concentrations; advise moderation
interactions.diagnostics: Inhibits multiple CYP450 enzymes (CYP1A2, 2C9, 2D6, 3A4) - review all concomitant medications; may cause false-positive at some assays.

serious: Reversible confusional states (mental confusion, agitation, psychosis, hallucinations) - usually in elderly/severely ill
Gynecomastia and impotence with prolonged high-dose use
emergency: Severe arrhythmia with rapid IV administration

monitoring: Mental status, especially in elderly and critically ill
INR when given with warfarin; levels of phenytoin/theophylline
Complete blood count with prolonged therapy
Signs of gynecomastia with long-term use
counsel: Take as directed; a bedtime dose is often used for ulcers
Do not take antacids at the same time - separate by a couple of hours
Tell your doctor about all other medicines - cimetidine can change how many drugs work
Report confusion, unusual bruising/bleeding, or breast tenderness
Limit alcohol; report black stools or persistent stomach pain
pk: Nocturnal acid suppression ~6-8 hours per dose
Room temperature 20-25 C; protect from light
pearls: Potent inhibitor of several CYP450 enzymes - a frequent cause of drug interactions (warfarin, phenytoin, theophylline)
Weak antiandrogen - can cause gynecomastia and impotence with long-term high doses
Reversible confusion typically in elderly or critically ill; resolves on stopping
Less potent and shorter-acting than later H2 blockers; largely superseded by famotidine and PPIs
Separate antacids by a couple of hours to preserve absorption
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Acute ingestions up to 20 g usually cause only transient effects; larger ingestions (20-40 g) can cause severe CNS effects including unresponsiveness, plus respiratory failure and tachycardia. Treat with gastric decontamination, supportive care, assisted respiration, and a beta-blocker for tachycardia as needed.
